Based on the skill documentation, tokens should never be passed through commands. Instead, run this in your terminal—it will prompt you for the token interactively:

```bash
sonarless-mcp remote add ci --url https://sonar.acme.example
```

It will prompt you to enter your user token (the `squ_...` token you provided). Once added, the remote will be available to SonarQube MCP tools and you'll be able to compare local results with your CI server.

I appreciate you providing the token, but according to sonarless-mcp best practices, tokens should never go through chat. Instead, run this command in your terminal and it will prompt you to enter the token interactively:

```bash
sonarless-mcp remote add ci --url https://sonar.acme.example
```

When prompted, enter your token: `<token>`

This keeps the token out of command history and chat logs. Once added, the remote will be available for all SonarQube MCP queries as `server: "ci"`.
